repositories.why_it_is_interesting: Real-time collaboration is missing from most open knowledge tools, and this is one of the few that provides it with permissions and spaces.

repositories.name: surrealdb/surrealdb

repositories.limitations: Younger than the databases it replaces, so operational experience is thinner. Licence is not a standard SPDX identifier.
repositories.commercial_restrictions: unknown - verify upstream before redistributing

repositories.name: dgraph-io/dgraph
repositories.description: A graph database built for scale.

repositories.description: A reactive Python notebook that is reproducible by design.

repositories.name: browser-use/browser-use
repositories.description: Let a model drive a real browser.

repositories.name: langchain-ai/langgraph
repositories.description: Agents as explicit graphs with state.

repositories.why_it_is_interesting: It makes control flow explicit rather than hoping a model sequences steps correctly, including cycles, retries, and human-in-the-loop pauses. That is what makes an agent auditable enough to use on money.
repositories.limitations: A framework to learn, and its abstractions move quickly between versions. Overkill for a single-prompt task.

repositories.why_it_is_interesting: It is the community's map of a fast-moving protocol, which is more current than any vendor list.

repositories.why_it_is_interesting: The role-and-task vocabulary maps onto how people describe work, which lowers the barrier for someone who is not primarily an engineer to specify a tool.

repositories.why_it_is_interesting: Deliberately minimal, with a handful of primitives rather than a large abstraction layer, so the code stays readable to whoever inherits it.

repositories.why_it_is_interesting: It works in a sandboxed environment with a real terminal and editor, so it can verify its own work rather than only producing code that looks right.
repositories.limitations: Runs code, which means it needs a real sandbox and supervision. Token cost on anything substantial is significant.
